title: Quarterly planning for the platform reliability and developer experience groups, with an honestly far too long title

blocks.text: Quarterly planning for the platform reliability and developer experience groups, with an honestly far too long title

Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious-hyphenated-compound-words-that-never-end sit next to a path with no spaces: /Users/someone/Projects/a-very-long-folder-name/with/many/nested/levels/and/a/file-name-that-goes-on-and-on.txt
We will move the build cache to the new storage cluster in March, which should cut cold starts in half without any extra cost.
The on-call rotation stays at four people, and nobody carries the pager two weeks in a row.
Incident reviews happen within five working days, and every action item gets an owner and a date.
We measure developer experience with a quarterly survey and the median time from merge to production.
Hiring two more engineers lets us finish the migration by June, assuming nothing else slips.
Every service gets an error budget, and a team that spends it stops shipping features until it recovers.
The last paragraph closes the plan: we review it again at the end of the quarter, with the numbers.

messages.text: That depends on where the cold starts come from. If most of them are image pulls, a faster cache helps; if they are scheduler waits, it changes nothing. Do you have the split from the last month, and how would you check it before March?
We have the split for October: about seventy percent of the time is the image pull, and the rest is the scheduler and the network setup put together.
Then the cache is the right lever, but say so in the plan, with the October number.
Moving to a new cluster has a cost: the cluster itself, and the migration time.

threads.mind_name: The extraordinarily meticulous principal engineer who reads every line

messages.text: Four people means each one is on call one week in four. Is that sustainable with the new services?

threads.quote: nobody carries the pager two weeks in a row

messages.text: Who covers when someone is on leave?
Why five? What happens on day six?

threads.quote: every action item gets an owner and a date

messages.text: Who checks that the dates are met?
A quarterly survey has four data points a year. Is that enough to steer by?

threads.quote: median time from merge to production

messages.text: Why the median and not the tail?
Two new engineers take about three months to be productive, so June is tight.
Who decides when it has recovered?
Define error budget once, for readers outside the team.
